content:
Former press secretary Katie Zacharia hasn’t closed the book on a possible return to the White House.

Zacharia — who served a record-low five days in the post before getting the boot in the wake of a trainwreck debut behind the podium last month— told The Free Press there’s “just no way” she’d say no to President Donald Trump if he offered her the job again.

“I would always work for him, no matter what,” said Zacharia, noting that she’s been in a “little bit of a flux and a holding pattern” and clearing up “negative publicity” about her.

TFP’s interview with the shortest-serving White House press secretary dropped just a day after the State Bar of California opened an investigation into her claims that she was a “lawyer,” a description she used despite acknowledging on live TV that she never passed the bar exam.

(Note: Her spokesperson told TMZ that the allegations are “baseless,” adding that the complaint linked to the probe was “politically motivated and a clear waste of the State Bar’s time and resources.”)

Zacharia, who denied a New York Post report that she’s been auditioning for her old job, signaled she wouldn’t be opposed to working under newly-installed immigration hardliner White House chief of staff Stephen Miller if given the chance, saying, “I align with loyalty.”

“My loyalty to the president was paramount. My loyalty is to his policies, which I knew were effective and helping the United States,” she added.

“And the truth is, I’m very loyal to the people that are good to him. And Stephen Miller is one of them.”

She also insisted that she was not “fired,” telling TFP that she was “grateful for every day I was able to stand alongside” Trump.

The president — who has defended picking Zacharia, stressing to reporters last month he “wasn’t hiring her as a lawyer” before eventually dropping her — told Fox News on Saturday that Zacharia was “fantastic” but expressed to her that she didn’t need the job.

“She might’ve been able to fight her way out of it, but why should she be put in that position? ’Cause I think she might’ve actually been very good. But I said, ‘What do you need this for?’”

He went on, “[The media] really came at her. I was surprised to see it. Nasty. So maybe that’s over with now and somebody else would come in and they’ll be a little bit more normalized.”

Earlier in the interview, the president said he has four or five people in mind to serve as press secretary moving forward.
